# BASE IMAGE: Use the specified base image which includes Flux, OpenMPI, and AWS EFA support for ARM64.
FROM ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-openmpi:ubuntu2204-efa-arm

# Set environment variables for non-interactive installation
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Set OSU benchmarks version as a build argument for easy updates
ARG OSU_VERSION=7.3

# Install build dependencies, download tools, and certificates.
# Then, download, compile, and install the OSU Micro-Benchmarks.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    automake \
    autoconf \
    libtool && \
    #
    # Download and extract the OSU Micro-Benchmarks source code
    #
    cd /tmp && \
    wget "https://mvapich.cse.ohio-state.edu/download/mvapich/osu-micro-benchmarks-${OSU_VERSION}.tar.gz" && \
    tar -zxf "osu-micro-benchmarks-${OSU_VERSION}.tar.gz" && \
    cd "osu-micro-benchmarks-${OSU_VERSION}" && \
    #
    # Configure the build to use the MPI compilers provided by the base image
    #
    ./configure CC=mpicc CXX=mpicxx --prefix=/usr/local && \
    #
    # Compile the benchmarks
    #
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    #
    # Install the compiled executables into a system location on the PATH (/usr/local/bin)
    #
    make install && \
    #
    # Clean up the build artifacts and source code to reduce image size
    #
    cd / && \
    rm -rf /tmp/* && \
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Set a default command to verify that a key benchmark is in the PATH
CMD ["which", "osu_allreduce"]

flux-minicluster-manifest.item:
# This MiniCluster manifest is designed to run the OSU AllReduce benchmark
# across 4 nodes on an AWS EKS cluster with ARM-based instances (e.g., Graviton)
# and EFA (Elastic Fabric Adapter) enabled for high-performance networking.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # A descriptive name for the MiniCluster job.
  name: flux-osu-allreduce-aws-arm
  # The job will be deployed to the default namespace.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The total number of pods in the MiniCluster.
  # This will schedule 4 pods, one per node, for the benchmark.
  size: 4

  # The total number of MPI tasks. Here we map one task per pod.
  tasks: 4

  # Enforce strict schema validation for the CRD.
  logging:
    strict: true

  # Do not delete pods and other resources after the job completes.
  # This is useful for debugging and inspecting logs.
  cleanup: false

  # Flux Operator specific configurations.
  flux:
    # Specify the architecture is ARM, required for AWS Graviton instances.
    arch: "arm"
    container:
      # Use the ARM-compatible flux-view image for the operator's helper container.
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-ubuntu:arm-jammy
      # IMPORTANT: This disables the flux-container wrapper.
      # This is necessary to allow the application container to directly access
      # host-level network devices like AWS EFA. The flux binary must
      # be present in the main application container image.
      disable: true

  # Define the application container to be run.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:osu-allreduce
      # Ensure the latest version of the container is always pulled.
      imagePullPolicy: Always

      # The command to execute. The Flux Operator will automatically wrap this
      # with 'flux run -n <tasks> ...'. Do not add 'flux run' here.
      command: osu_allreduce

      # This is the main application container, not a launcher pod.
      # This MUST be false.
      launcher: false

      # Requesting AWS EFA resources. This tells Kubernetes to schedule the pod
      # only on nodes that have an EFA device available.
      resources:
        limits:
          vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: "1"
        requests:
          vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: "1"

context.environment: AWS CPU instance in Kubernetes to run across nodes
context.details:
You MUST use ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-openmpi:ubuntu2204-efa-arm as a base image. It includes OpenMPI and libfabric provided from the efa installer for AWS and the entire Flux Framework stack.
You MUST compile setting the cxx compiler to mpicxx and the c compiler to mpicc.
Build the OSU benchmarks. You MUST have MPI support enabled. You MUST ensure osu_allreduce is on the path.
You MUST build for a multi-node MPI environment

context.resources: The resource spec you got earlier is for an autoscaling cluster, so the nodes possible are not there. You must add the nodeSelector to use node.kubernetes.io/instance-type m7g.16xlarge with 64 CPU, 256 GiB Memory, ARM (Graviton3). You are limited to up to 4 nodes.
context.details:
Run The OSU All Reduce benchmark across 4 nodes. 
You MUST run on up to 4 nodes and you MUST set flux.container.disable to true.
You MUST set the containers imagePullPolicy to Always.
The Flux Operator uses flux run in the pwd with the tasks determined by the spec.tasks.
You MUST set resource requests and limits to use vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: 1
Since this is an ARM instance you MUST change the flux.container.image to be
ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-ubuntu:arm-jammy and set flux.arch: "arm".
